text.p: The Australian government has released draft legislation for the deregulation of the telecommunications industry from July 1997.
The government said it hoped to formally introduce the telecommunications bill into parliament in November and would like it to pass the upper house, the Senate, before the end of the year.
The draft plans have been released in three stages since August 16 with the third tranche released last Tuesday, and are now open for industry comment.
Key details of the draft legislation are:
-- telecommunications carriers are not permitted to introduce timed local calls, except in the case of business users of the Internet and other data-based services;
-- the analogue mobile phone network will be phased out by the year 2000;

-- the government will retain a safety net to ensure rural consumers are not disadvantaged by the phase-out of analogue phones, under which the communications minister can seek an exemption for certain areas;
-- the current price cap on state-owned carrier Telstra Corp will remain until at least December 1998;
-- consumers will have the ability to choose their preferred telecommunications service provider and to override that choice on a call-by-call basis;
-- consumers with a standard telephone service will have the option of itemised billing;
-- anyone will have the right to install telecommunications infrastructure for their own use and will only have to apply for a licence in order to supply services to the public;
-- a person with a telecommunications line of more than 500 metres or a total network longer than five km also requires a licence;
-- licensed carriers will have to pay fees for industry regulation and will have to share facilities such as underground ducts, poles, towers, and system data;
-- carriers will have to allow others connections to their networks;
-- Australian Competition and Consumer Commission is to have wide powers to resolve any disputes; and,
-- the communications minister will have the power to set up principles on which access prices are determined.
